sparse_delta_c.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Sec. 7.3, Theorem 15, Eqs. (7.57)-(7.58) and p. 126 ('Delta_c = 1/(2 log 2)'; notes.txt lines 7600-7726; the extraction's 'Delta <= 1/2 log 2' is 1/(2 log 2), confirmed by Eq. (7.92) and the PDF): the symbolic threshold (no decimal is printed), evaluated with mpmath at 50 digits, rounded to 30. Convention: y = x* + sqrt(Delta/N) z, x* one of the d = 2^N basis vectors (KZ Eq. (7.51)).
sparse_delta_c.independent_route: the REM route: the d - 1 wrong components form a REM at N_scale = 1/2, beta = sqrt(2/Delta) (families/rem.py), whose beta_c = 2 sqrt(ln 2) maps to Delta_c = 2/beta_c^2 (bayes/sparse_vector.py free_entropy_via_rem; tests/test_bayes_scalar.py)

sparse_f_delta_half.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Sec. 7.3, Theorem 15, Eq. (7.57): f(Delta) = 1/(2 Delta) - log 2 for Delta <= Delta_c (printed, a theorem proved in the notes by the bounds of Lemmas 8-9, whose labels 'Upper bound' / 'Lower bound' are swapped); the value is its evaluation at Delta = 1/2 (1 - log 2), mpmath at 50 digits rounded to 30. Convention as sparse_delta_c.
sparse_f_delta_half.independent_route: the REM route max(1/(2 Delta) - log 2, -log 2 - 1/(2 Delta) - beta f_REM(beta)) with beta = sqrt(2/Delta) (families/rem.py); the exact finite-d (1/N) E log Z by quadrature and by direct sampling over named seeds at N = 10 (tests/test_bayes_scalar.py)
